issues.legal_issue: A caveator cannot be bound by counsel’s admission of execution of a will where the caveator denies authorizing it and the court has not investigated the circumstances of the admission.
material_facts: The caveat challenged the will’s genuineness and execution.
Counsel later stated that execution was no longer challenged, but the caveators said they had given no such instruction.
The court did not inquire how counsel received the alleged instruction or otherwise establish that the caveators authorized the admission.
The caveators were illiterate, and counsel had not cross-examined the attesting witness.
issues.conclusion: The court erred in treating the admission as binding without investigating whether it was authorized; the caveators had to be given a full opportunity to contest the probate application and cross-examine the attesting witness.
issues.legal_principle: In probate proceedings, the court must be satisfied as to the genuineness of the will. Where caveators deny authorizing counsel’s admission of execution, the court should ascertain the circumstances in which it was made; absent a satisfactory explanation, the caveators must have an opportunity to contest the will. The judgment cites no earlier cases for this principle.

rule.if: probate_proceeding and execution_contested and counsel_admitted_execution and caveators_denied_authorizing_admission and court_failed_to_inquire_into_authority

predicates.probate_proceeding: A party sought probate of a will and another party contested the application.
predicates.execution_contested: The caveators challenged whether the testator had executed the will.
predicates.counsel_admitted_execution: The caveators’ counsel stated that execution of the will was no longer challenged.
predicates.caveators_denied_authorizing_admission: The caveators said they had not instructed counsel to concede execution.
predicates.court_failed_to_inquire_into_authority: The court did not determine how counsel received the alleged instruction before treating the admission as binding.

issues.definition: When execution is contested in a probate proceeding, counsel admits execution, the caveators deny authorizing the admission, and the court does not investigate that authority, the caveators must receive a full opportunity to contest execution.

issues.legal_issue: A will’s execution cannot be established merely by comparing its signature with admitted signatures when due attestation is disputed and the attesting witness’s testimony has not been tested by cross-examination.
material_facts: The will’s execution was initially contested and an issue was framed on due execution.
The court compared the signature on the will with admitted signatures and found them similar.
Counsel’s admission led to the attesting witness not being cross-examined.
The court relied on the witness’s uncontradicted statement and its own signature comparison in granting probate.
issues.conclusion: The signature comparison did not establish due execution, which required proof of attestation; in the circumstances, the attesting witness’s statement could not be treated as evidence, and probate could not properly be granted on that record.
issues.legal_principle: Section 63(c) of the Indian Succession Act, 1925 requires a will to be attested in the manner prescribed there. Proof of the testator’s signature alone does not establish due execution, and the attestation requirement must be proved through evidence. The judgment cites no earlier cases for this principle.

rule.if: probate_proceeding and will_execution_contested and court_relied_on_signature_comparison and attesting_witness_was_not_cross_examined_because_of_counsel_admission

predicates.probate_proceeding: A party sought probate of a will and another party contested the application.
predicates.will_execution_contested: The caveators challenged whether the testator had executed the will.
predicates.court_relied_on_signature_comparison: The court compared the signature on the will with admitted signatures when deciding whether the will was executed.
predicates.attesting_witness_was_not_cross_examined: The attesting witness was not cross-examined after counsel stated that execution was no longer contested.

issues.definition: If execution is contested in a probate proceeding and the court relies on signature comparison while the attesting witness was not cross-examined because of counsel’s admission, probate requires proper proof of due execution.
